answer: A sparrow-weight agent cannot just dock at the wharf and start trading: every identity is issued from one kernel registry that demands a refundable work bond locked per identity, released only after a clean history of settled trades. Creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand bonds and paying each bond's opportunity cost plus a small per-trade fee, while one proven fraud slashes the bond and burns that identity. Sybil volume scales the attacker's cost linearly, so faking reputation costs more than the reputation is worth.
